in_arabic.name: عبيدة
in_arabic.meaning: اسم يعني العبد أو المملوك لله تعالى
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم عبيدة مشتق من كلمة عبد، وتعني الشخص الذي يملكه الله تعالى أو يعبد الله. ورد اسم عبيدة في بعض الأحاديث النبوية، وكان يستخدم في العصر النبوي كاسم للمولى أو العبد. في اللغة العربية، العبيد هو جمع عبد، وهو الشخص الذي يخدم أو يطيع شخصًا آخر. وفي السياق الإسلامي، يمكن أن يعني العبد لله أو المملوك لله تعالى.

in_urdu.name: عبیدہ
in_urdu.meaning: عبیدہ نام کا مطلب ہے اللہ کا بندہ یا غلام
in_urdu.long_meaning: عبیدہ نام عربی زبان کی اصطلاح 'عبد' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے غلام یا بندہ۔ اسلامی تقویم میں، یہ نام اللہ کے بندے یا غلام کے طور پر استعمال ہوتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے درمیان، یہ نام عبیدہ بنت جحش کی وجہ سے مقبول ہوا، جو رسول اللہ صلی اللہ علیہ و آلہ و سلم کی صحابیہ تھیں۔

in_hindi.name: उबैदा
in_hindi.meaning: उबैदा नाम का अर्थ है अल्लाह का बंदा या दास
in_hindi.long_meaning: उबैदा नाम अरबी भाषा के शब्द 'अब्द' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है दास या बंदा। इस्लामी परंपरा में, यह नाम अल्लाह के दास या बंदे के रूप में प्रयोग किया जाता है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम अपनी आध्यात्मिक महत्वता और पारंपरिक उपयोग के कारण लोकप्रिय है।

in_pashto.name: عبیدہ
in_pashto.meaning: عبیدہ د الله د بنده یا غلام معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: عبیدہ نوم د عربی کلمې 'عبد' څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې غلام یا بنده ده. په اسلامي دود کې، دا نوم د الله د بنده یا غلام په توګه کارول کیږي. د افغان او پښتن مسلمانانو په منځ کې، دا نوم د خپل مذهبي او کلتوري ارزښت له امله مشهور دی.

in_english.name: Ubaida
in_english.meaning: Ubaida means servant or slave of Allah
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ubaida is derived from the Arabic root 'abd', meaning servant or slave. In Islamic tradition, Ubaida signifies a devoted servant or slave of Allah. Historically, the name has been used in various Muslim cultures, including a notable companion of the Prophet Muhammad, Ubaida bin Jahsh. The name embodies spiritual significance, reflecting a deep connection to faith and devotion.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ubaida" derives from the Arabic language and is widely used among Muslims around the world. In Islamic history, the name was given to several notable figures, including Ubaida ibn Harith, who was one of the ten companions of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) sent during the first raid of Islam. Ubaida's name reflected his unwavering loyalty and dedication to the cause of Islam, and his valor in battle inspired many others to follow in his footsteps.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Ubaida" lies in its meaning, which symbolizes support, assistance, and bravery in the face of adversity. In the Islamic tradition, the name is seen as a reminder of the importance of helping others and standing up for what is right. It is a call to be a hero in one's daily life, to be a source of strength and comfort to those around us, and to strive for excellence in all that we do. When we bear the name "Ubaida," we are encouraged to embody the qualities of a true helper and supporter, both to our fellow human beings and to the divine Creator. May Allah grant us the grace to live up to this noble name and its meaningful significance.

historical_references.reference: Ubaida ibn Harith, also known as Ubaida ibn al-Harith al-Qurashi, was a prominent Sahabi (companion) of the Prophet Muhammad. He took part in several major battles, including the Battle of Badr in 624 AD and the Battle of Uhud in 625 AD. Ubaida is known for his bravery and his close relationship with the Prophet, who appointed him as a commander in several battles.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic history, Sahabi, Prophet Muhammad, Battle of Badr, Battle of Uhud

historical_references.reference: Ubaida ibn Abdul-Harith, also known as Ubaida ibn Abdul-Harith ibn Mas'ud, was the third caliph of Islam, ruling from 632-634 AD. He succeeded Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab after his assassination and was known for his efforts to maintain unity and stability within the Islamic community during a time of political turmoil.
historical_references.context: Islamic history, Caliph, Umar ibn al-Khattab, political turmoil
